da-non-sequitur.evidence: [first real review 2026-11-21; no hashed entry existed] I checked the proof by hand. The odd step P -> ([3]P+1)/[2] and the even step P -> P/[2] compose to A P + B with A = [3]^k_odd / [2]^k. With A = 1 the cycle condition forces B = 0, but B is a nonempty sum of positive terms when k_odd >= 1, so B > 0 at every real q > 0 and B is nonzero in Q(q). Coprimality: [3] - q[2] = 1, so [3] is congruent to 1 mod [2], and [2] = 1+q is not a unit in Z[q] or Z[q^+-1]; hence [3]^a = [2]^k has no solution with a, k >= 1 there. The plastic-number example also checks: rho^3 = rho + 1 gives [2] = rho^3 and [3] = rho^5, so [3]^3 = [2]^5 = rho^15. The proof matches the re-scoped statement (balanced-holonomy case only), and the Scope paragraph correctly leaves the A != 1 case open. Minor: 'b_i = 1/[2]_q^{.}' has a stray exponent placeholder; on an odd step b_i = 1/[2]_q.
